title: Carton shortfall found at port gate
finding: Verified carton count was lower than the packing list after the container reached the port gate. Loading tally at the factory did not match the gate count.
checks: Recount cartons against the packing list
Compare the factory loading tally with the gate count
Check container seal numbers at loading and at the gate
Hold release until the recount is done

title: RFID read at gate while truck GPS showed another place
finding: The tag was read at the gate but the truck GPS fix was far away. The GPS device had stopped reporting earlier in the trip.
checks: Match the truck plate with the gate log
Check the last ping time and battery of the GPS device
Check the exact time of the tag read
Treat tracking data as unverified until confirmed

title: Quantity shortfall together with RFID and GPS disagreement
finding: Unverified units and conflicting position data appeared on the same shipment. Because both signals were wrong at once, the team treated it as a possible handover or loading problem.
checks: Escalate to a supervisor and start a physical verification
Compare seal numbers and review gate camera footage
Ask the forwarder for the handover record
Record the human decision and the reason in the audit log

title: Truck left the planned highway route
finding: The shipment moved off the planned Dhaka to Chattogram route. The driver company later confirmed a road diversion.
checks: Call the transport dispatcher and ask for the reason
Check whether an alternate route was approved
Update the expected arrival time

title: Delay caused by yard congestion at the port
finding: Arrival was later than expected because trucks queued at the port yard before gate-in.
checks: Check the yard and berth schedule
Check the vessel cut-off time
Decide with the forwarder whether to rebook

title: Route deviation followed by delay
finding: The shipment left its route and then arrived behind schedule. The sensors agreed with each other, so the data was trusted while the shipment itself was late.
checks: Confirm the reason for the deviation with dispatch
Recalculate the arrival time
Warn the buyer if the vessel cut-off is at risk

title: GPS signal gap on a long leg
finding: No GPS update arrived for a long period, then the position jumped. The scan times and the delay did not fit together.
checks: Find the last known position and time
Check the device status and coverage on that leg
Do not assume loss or theft from a signal gap alone

title: False alarm: reader maintenance caused a scan gap
finding: An alert was raised for missing scans, but port operations later confirmed the reader was under maintenance. Nothing was wrong with the cargo.
checks: Confirm with port operations before escalating
Mark the alert as a false positive after the human review
Keep the decision in the audit log for later review
